Fact.Name: Schedule 1 Part II adjustments before the self-employed health insurance deduction
Fact.Description:
Adjustments to income EXCLUDING three of the printed Schedule 1 Part II lines: the IRA deduction (line 20), the student loan interest deduction (line 21) and the self-employed health insurance deduction (line 17). It is the body of /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra with the line 17 term left out, and that fact is now this subtotal plus line 17.
THIS SUBTOTAL IS A RE-ASSOCIATION OF /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra's OWN ADD, WITH NO VALUE CHANGE: every addend here stands in that fact's Add in the same order with its own comment carried across, and the line 17 term sits one level up, in the parent's Add. There is no Round on either side of the split, because the single Round of this chain lives at /adjustmentsToIncome, so the split re-associates one Dollar Add and nothing else: /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra, /adjustmentsToIncome, /agi and every MAGI built on AGI are byte-identical for every committed scenario and every committed node fixture. This fact adds no addend and drops none.
WHY THE SPLIT EXISTS. Publication 974's simplified calculation method needs the Schedule 1 adjustments subtotal WITHOUT line 17 (Worksheet X line 4), because line 17 is the quantity that worksheet is solving for: a Worksheet X built on /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra would read scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction and close a resolution cycle through the very deduction it computes. form7206:/pub974WorksheetXLine8TaxpayerModifiedAgi is that Pub 974 Worksheet consumer; the parent fact this was extracted from is the other.

Adjustments to income EXCLUDING both the IRA deduction (Schedule 1, line 20) and the student loan interest deduction (line 21): the sum of Schedule 1 lines 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19a, 23 and 25. This is the base for the IRA-deduction modified-AGI (which must NOT subtract the IRA deduction) and the body of /adjustmentsToIncomeExcludingStudentLoanInterest. Of these lines, the educator (11), HSA (13), reservist/performing-artist/fee-basis-official business expenses (12), Armed Forces moving expenses (14), deductible SE-tax (15), self-employed SEP/SIMPLE/qualified plans (16), self-employed health insurance (17), penalty on early withdrawal of savings (18), alimony paid (19a), the Archer MSA deduction (23) and — as the whole of line 25, "Add lines 24a through 24z" — the Form 2555 housing deduction (24j) plus the other eleven line 24 intakes are in scope. The lines with no adjustment intake of their own (12, 14, 16, 23 and the ten non-24j components of 25) are each read through a complete-safe OrZero wrapper in their own home module, so a return that never answers one adds a hard $0 and this subtotal — and every MAGI built on it — stays Complete rather than going Incomplete.
THE BODY IS TWO TERMS: /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanIraAndSelfEmployedHealthInsurance, which holds every addend above except line 17, and the line 17 self-employed health insurance term itself. The split is a re-association of one Dollar Add with no Round on either side, so this fact, /adjustmentsToIncome, /agi and every MAGI built on AGI are unaffected by it.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 Part II adjustments allowable after the Pub. 1321 territory apportionment
Fact.Description:
Total adjustments to income, apportioned by the Publication 570/1321 fraction when the return excludes section 931/933 territory income, and /adjustmentsToIncomeBeforeTerritoryApportionment unchanged otherwise. It is the amount Form 1040 line 10 prints (/adjustmentsToIncome reads it) and so the amount AGI subtracts.
THE RULE IS PRINTED, AND IT IS TWO RULES. Publication 1321: "You cannot take any deductions from Part II of Schedule 1 (Adjustments to Income) DIRECTLY RELATED to excluded Puerto Rico Income. For example, you cannot deduct one-half of self-employment tax (Schedule SE) if you are excluding your self-employment income (Schedule C). Adjustments to income which are NOT directly related to excluded Puerto Rico income must be allocated using the formula for allocating the standard deduction shown above" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 6). So: directly-related adjustments are DISALLOWED OUTRIGHT; the rest are APPORTIONED. This fact implements the second limb.
THE FIRST LIMB IS LIVE: the printed example — the deductible half of self-employment tax when the Schedule C income is excluded — is a real population once a possession-source income intake exists, and this fact, /magiForIraDeduction and ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion are the three facts that population touches.
⚠ THE DOUBLE-APPORTIONMENT THIS FACT MUST NOT COMMIT. scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction is an addend of /adjustmentsToIncomeBeforeTerritoryApportionment, and it is ALREADY apportioned — by Publication 570 chapter 4's SELF-EMPLOYMENT fraction, which is a different fraction over a different denominator (self-employment income, not gross income). Multiplying the whole total by the gross-income fraction after that would apply two fractions to one adjustment and cut it roughly twice. DIRECTION: deduction too SMALL, AGI too high, tax too high — taxpayer-ADVERSE, and wrong under both publications. SO THE TWO LIMBS ARE NOW SEPARATED IN THE BODY, which is what Publication 1321's sentence actually asks for: the half-SE-tax deduction is REMOVED from the apportioned base, the remainder takes the gross-income fraction, and the half-SE-tax deduction is added back at the amount its own rule already produced. The publication calls the first limb a DISALLOWANCE; Publication 570 chapter 4 refines it for the PARTIAL case ("If only part of your self-employment income is excluded, the part of the deduction that is based on the nonexcluded income is allowed", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 33), and the two agree at the endpoint because the self-employment fraction goes to zero when everything is excluded. ADDENDS CLASSIFIED AGAINST PUBLICATION 1321'S DIRECTLY-RELATED TEST: the student loan interest adjustment (section 221, a personal interest deduction attached to no income item), the HSA deduction (section 223, attached to coverage rather than income), the half-SE-tax deduction (DIRECTLY RELATED — the publication's own example), deductible alimony paid (section 215, attached to a payment), the Form 2555 line 50 housing deduction (which cannot co-exist with a section 931/933 exclusion — form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses the section 911 population outright), the educator-expenses adjustment (section 62(a)(2)(D)), and the Schedule 1 line 18 penalty on early withdrawal of savings (interest:/schedule1Line18EarlyWithdrawalPenalty, section 62(a)(9)): NOT-directly-related and therefore APPORTIONED with the remainder. The early-withdrawal deduction is allowed by section 165 for a forfeiture — a transaction entered into for profit — rather than by an income section. EXCEPT a penalty on a deposit whose interest the filer answers is excluded territory income (interest:/earlyWithdrawalPenaltyOnExcludedTerritoryInterest, a per-Form-1099-INT question): that penalty is DIRECTLY RELATED to excluded income, so the body lifts it out of the apportioned base and does not add it back - disallowed, as the publication says.
THE SECTION 162(l) SELF-EMPLOYED HEALTH INSURANCE DEDUCTION STAYS APPORTIONED. Section 1.861-8(e)(9)(iii) of the regulations, which section 1.933-1(c) points to, lists the deduction for medical expenses as not definitely related to any gross income and ratably apportioned; the section 162(l) deduction is a deduction for medical-care insurance. What ties it to self-employment income is its LIMIT, and that limit is where the exclusion now acts: section 401(c)(2)(A)(iv) figures the earned income of section 162(l)(2)(A) without regard to excluded items, so form7206:/form7206Line12TerritoryExcludedEarnedIncome takes the excluded Schedule C profit off Form 7206 line 13.
A THIRD NAMED GAP: /adjustmentsToIncomeBeforeTerritoryApportionment has grown addends this walk has not yet individually classified against the directly-related test — the IRA deduction terms, the reservist/ performing-artist/fee-basis-official business expenses, the Armed Forces moving expenses, the self-employed SEP/SIMPLE/qualified-plan deduction, and the Archer MSA deduction. The self-employed SEP/SIMPLE/qualified-plan deduction in particular is computed from self-employment net earnings the same way the flagged health-insurance deduction is, and may carry the same directly-related character on an excluded-self-employment-income return; this has not been checked against the publication and is not yet reflected in this fact's body.
WHY THE REMAINDER'S APPORTIONMENT LANDS ON THE SUBTOTAL rather than per adjustment: the publication says "adjustments to income ... must be allocated using the formula", naming the class rather than any line, and every REMAINING adjustment falls in the not-directly- related limb by the walk above. Apportioning the subtotal and apportioning each addend give the same figure up to one rounding, and the sum is what Schedule 1 line 26 carries into Form 1040 line 10.
DIRECTION OF THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES: adjustments allowed in full reduce AGI too much, which makes taxable income too low and tax too low — taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same class as every other limb of this work.
NO CYCLE, CHECKED: the fraction reads income:/grossIncomeSubjectToUsTax and income:/writableGrossIncomeFromAllSources — a derived fact over the ctcOdc exclusion aliases and an attestation, neither of which reads AGI or this module — and standardDeduction:/hasPossessionExclusionProration, whose module reads filers, filingStatus, form4684 and income only. AGI depends on this fact; nothing this fact depends on touches AGI. scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction introduces NO new module edge — /adjustmentsToIncomeBeforeTerritoryApportionment already sums it — and its own inputs (scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit and the two Schedule SE line 3s) read scheduleC, scheduleE and scheduleF, none of which touches AGI.
Complete-safe by construction: with no exclusion, or with the gross-income denominator unanswered, this IS /adjustmentsToIncomeBeforeTerritoryApportionment, so no committed return moves. The two-limb split does not change that: it is inside the apportioned arm, and on every committed node-test fixture that reaches that arm the half-SE-tax deduction is $0, so the subtraction and the add-back cancel exactly.

Fact.Name: Modified Adjusted Gross Income for Student Loan Interest Deduction
Fact.Description:
The section 221(b)(2)(C) modified AGI: total income, minus the Schedule 1 adjustments other than the student loan interest deduction itself, PLUS the section 911, 931 and 933 exclusions. Publication 970 Worksheet 4-1 lines 4 through 9.
THIS FACT IS NOT WORKSHEET LINE 4 OF THE IN-INSTRUCTIONS WORKSHEET — "This is AGI, but without student loan interest deduction. Line 4 of the Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet used for Schedule 1" — because that worksheet is the WRONG WORKSHEET for a filer who excludes section 911/931/933 income. The instructions say so in as many words: "Exception. Use Pub. 970 instead of the worksheet in these instructions to figure your student loan interest deduction if you file Form 2555 or 4563, or you exclude income from sources within Puerto Rico" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 98, reflowed down one column of a three-column extraction, so the sentence is a RANGE and appears on no single line). Worksheet 4-1 carries the same lines 1-4, then FOUR MORE ADDENDS the in-instructions worksheet does not have, and its line 9 — not its line 4 — is the modified AGI.
THE FOUR ADDENDS, and which fact each is: line 5, the foreign earned income and housing EXCLUSION (Schedule 1 line 8d), and line 6, the foreign housing DEDUCTION (Schedule 1 line 24j) — together ctcOdc /sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions, which is Form 2555 lines 45 and 50. Those are the same two quantities: form2555 /schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is line 45 NEGATED (Schedule 1 line 8d is entered as a negative figure) and /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction is line 50. Worksheet 4-1 line 9 says "Add lines 4 through 8", so the addend must be the POSITIVE magnitude; reading Schedule 1 line 8d literally would subtract the exclusion and invert the add-back. The ctcOdc alias is the positive form and is complete-safe, which the two form2555 facts are not on their own, so it is the one wired here. line 7, the section 933 Puerto Rico exclusion — ctcOdc /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933; line 8, the section 931 exclusion, Form 4563 line 15 — ctcOdc /possessionIncomeExclusion931. All three carry the IsComplete/Switch $0 tail, so an unanswered return produces exactly the number it produced before this rebody.
ARITHMETIC REASSOCIATED, VALUE IDENTICAL. Worksheet 4-1 computes line 4 = line 2 - line 3 and then line 9 = line 4 + lines 5 through 8. This body adds the four exclusion terms into the MINUEND instead: (line 2 + lines 5-8) - line 3. Integer cents throughout and no rounding between the two steps, so the two orders agree exactly. The worksheet's own order is what the transcript on the divergence witness walks. NO OUTER Round IS INTRODUCED — the pre-fill body carried none, and this MAGI drives a three-decimal proration where a rounding-placement change would be a value change in its own right.
DIRECTION OF THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES: omitting the add-backs UNDER-states MAGI, which SHRINKS the section 221(b)(2)(B) phaseout and makes the deduction TOO LARGE — taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same direction and the same class as every other section 931/933 MAGI surface in this dictionary. For example, the correct MAGI is 94,000, 9,000 into the 15,000 phaseout band, and the deduction is 1,000. An over-claim of 1,500 on one return.
OTHER MAGI-BEARING FACTS CHECKED AGAINST THEIR OWN AUTHORITY, recorded so the walk is not repeated: scheduleE /section8582Magi is CORRECT as it stands (section 469(i)(3)(E) names no exclusion section at all), and form8960 /niitMagi is CORRECT (section 1411(d) names section 911 alone, and the add-back is wired). /magiForIraDeduction's 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) reading is right (section 219(g)(3) names sections 135, 137, 221 and 911 and NOT 931 or 933, 26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024); that fact's own Description covers its own base. elderlyAndDisabled /edcMagi is not a section-931/933 surface either: Schedule R line 16 is plain AGI less the exemption amount.
RELATION TO ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion: this fact is one of the MAGI surfaces the Publication 570 chapter 4 apportionment reaches.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents. No floor: the worksheet prescribes none, and a negative line 4 is reachable through the adjustments.

Fact.Name: Modified Adjusted Gross Income for the IRA Deduction — Pub. 590-A Worksheet 1-1
Fact.Description:
The section 219(g)(3)(A) modified AGI for the traditional IRA deduction phaseout: adjusted gross income, computed without regard to the IRA deduction itself or the section 221 student loan interest deduction, and increased by the section 135 savings-bond interest through the gross-interest basis, plus the section 137 (employer-provided adoption benefits) and section 911 (foreign earned income and housing) exclusions — four of the five items section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) names besides the deduction under section 219 itself, the fifth being section 85(c) (below). Sections 85(c) and 931/933 are deliberately NOT in this list: section 85(c)'s unemployment-compensation exclusion has no TY2025 mechanism anywhere in this dictionary (nor in current law — it was a one-year 2020 provision), and section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) does not name sections 931 or 933 at all, so no possession-income add-back belongs in this MAGI even though the analogous section 86(b)(2) base for taxable social security carries one.
Matches Pub. 590-A Worksheet 1-1, "Figuring Your Modified AGI", line 7 (the sum of lines 1 through 6) exactly: line 1 is AGI without Schedule 1 line 20 (the IRA deduction), line 2 is the student loan interest deduction, lines 3-4 are the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion and housing exclusion/deduction, line 5 is the Form 8815 excludable savings bond interest. The gross-interest basis below already includes that amount, avoiding a separate line-5 addback and a dependency on the final Form 8815 line 14. Line 6 is the Form 8839 line 30 excluded employer-provided adoption benefit.
Built from the same acyclic leaf-fact list socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 uses for the analogous section 86(b)(2) base — never from that fact, from income:/totalIncome, or from this module's own /agi. For the Pub. 590-A Appendix B population, /totalIncome's line 6b term is Worksheet 3, which subtracts the Schedule 1 line 20 IRA deduction that this MAGI itself feeds; reading /totalIncome or /agi at any depth deadlocks dictionary load (a parked lazy-val, not an exception). The section 137 term is the same phaseout-independent substitution the SSBW uses: income:/employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 (Form 1040 line 1z without the two Form 8839 line 1f legs) plus form8839:/adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits (the GROSS benefit) is algebraically identical to Worksheet 1-1's own "AGI + line 30 excluded amount" — AGI's line 1f already carries the taxable remainder, so AGI + excluded = (income disregarding 137) + (remainder + excluded) = (income disregarding 137) + gross benefit — without ever reading the phaseout-dependent Form 8839 line 30/31 figures that section computes FROM this MAGI.
Type/sign/rounding: Dollar. One Round over the whole income-side sum, mirroring /totalIncome's own Round placement (the social security term is already rounded inside /plainSsbwTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits), then an unrounded subtraction of adjustments. Byte-identical to the pre-unit value for every committed scenario, none of which carries a section 135 exclusion or a possession-income exclusion.
CONSUMERS: iraDeduction:/iraDeductionModifiedAgi (which adds back the allowed section 501(c)(18) deduction, TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-301, and feeds both filers' phaseout) and form8815:/form8815ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome — the only two facts that read it. The section 911 term is ctcOdc:/sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions, read directly in the leaf list. No socialSecurity worksheet line 3 figure and no section 931 or 933 add-back is in that list; form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555 condition 6 says the same (the argument for verify row FED-1040-IRADED-F2555KOPROSE-045, ARGUE).

That fact takes the greater of Schedule B payer rounding and aggregate rounding before line 14, so it dominates either line-2b mode if the final exclusion is zero. This keeps the bound at least as large as the exact MAGI without a dependency on line 14, which is downstream of this IRA route.

Fact.Name: Taxable income
Fact.Description:
Taxable income as reported on line 15 of Form 1040: AGI less total deductions, never below zero, and never below a REMIC excess inclusion.
THE SECTION 860E FLOOR is the third GreaterOf arm. A holder of a residual interest in a REMIC reports a Schedule E Part IV column (c) excess inclusion, and that amount "is the smallest amount you are allowed to report as your taxable income (Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15)"; operatively, "If the amount in column (c) is larger than your taxable income would otherwise be, enter the amount from column (c) on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15." So it is a floor on this line, not a summand of income — folding it into Schedule E line 39 is forbidden by that form's own CAUTION and would over-state total income instead.
BYTE-IDENTICAL WHEN THERE IS NO EXCESS INCLUSION, and the proof is visible in the tree rather than argued: scheduleE:/scheduleERemicExcessInclusion is Complete 0 on every return that does not claim a residual interest or leaves the column unanswered, and it is NON-NEGATIVE by the Min 0 limit on its writable. The existing <Dollar>0 arm therefore already dominates it, so GreaterOf(x, 0, 0) = GreaterOf(x, 0) for every x. NOTE that the sibling floor site form6251:/alternativeMinimumTaxableIncome could NOT use this shape and needed an explicit guard instead: AMTI is signed, has no dominating zero arm, and a bare floor would have clamped a negative line 4 up to zero. The asymmetry is deliberate.
The boundary: column (c) of exactly 16,750 leaves the result unmoved, and 16,751 moves it by a dollar.

Fact.Name: Qualified business income deduction
Fact.Description:
Qualified business income deductions for line 13 of Form 1040. Which of the two QBI forms a return works is qbi:/qbiUsesForm8995A: Case 1 is the simplified Form 8995 computation, Case 2 is the full Form 8995-A W-2 wage / UBIA cap + SSTB path via /qbi8995aDeduction, and the catch-all is $0 (no QBI, or above the threshold with no Form 8995-A detail supplied). Routing is NOT keyed on /isAboveQbiThreshold alone: Form 8995's header excludes patrons from that form OUTRIGHT — "Use this form if your taxable income ... is at or below $197,300 ($394,600 if married filing jointly), and you aren't a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1) — and the Form 8995-A instructions list being a patron as an INDEPENDENT reason to use Form 8995-A (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 1), so a below-threshold patron must route to Form 8995-A, where /qbiSimplifiedAmount would otherwise see neither the Form 8995-A line-14 patron reduction nor the line-38 section 199A(g) DPAD. A below-threshold NON-patron takes Case 1 whether or not they answered /writableClaims8995A, because Case 1 is tested first and /qbiUsesForm8995A is false for them.
CASE 2 READS THE PER-ITEM QBI (/qualifiedBusinesses/*/qualifiedBusinessIncome), and that alias can itself carry the Schedule C derivation: an item whose /qualifiedBusinesses/*/linkedScheduleC link RESOLVES derives its QBI from the linked business, so Case 2 reaches the derivation through the alias exactly as Case 1's return-level fallback does — the two paths move together by construction. The completeness guard is ../hasQbiAnswer (an answered amount OR a resolving link), not a bare writable-answered test; an item with neither stays Incomplete and the return is refused.
THE REIT/PTP COMPONENT (Form 8995 lines 6-10) IS MODELED in Case 1: line 9's REIT and PTP component is added to line 5 INSIDE the line-15 smaller-of, per line 10 "Add lines 5 and 9" — outside it, the component would escape the 20%-of-taxable-income income limitation. It reads qbi:/qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome, the SAME intake Case 2 reaches through /qbi8995aDeduction's Form 8995-A lines 28-32, so a filer's REIT/PTP component does not change across the section 199A threshold. LINE 7, the prior-year REIT/PTP loss carryforward, is ALSO MODELED: qbi:/qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn, an attested carry-IN stored as a POSITIVE magnitude and SUBTRACTED inside the line-8 floor, complete-safe $0 when unanswered - an answered carryforward can only reduce the deduction. THE SAME alias feeds Form 8995-A line 29 through qbi:/qbi8995aDeduction — both consumers wired from one component, so it cannot be wired into only one of the two QBI paths and make the deduction jump at the threshold. Case 1's else-branch is taken whenever the filer reported no REIT/PTP amount at all.
THE INNER GATE has three disjuncts, because line 6 has three routes: the return-level writable, dividendReports:/section199ADividendsFromDividends (Form 1099-DIV box 5, tested strictly > $0, since a filer with a box-5 amount and a line-7 carryforward must not silently lose the carryforward), and qbi:/hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) item D plus the box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount, tested by EXISTENCE rather than magnitude, because qualified PTP income may itself be a LOSS and a PTP loss must select the arm too). This fact and qbi:/qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad both read the single qbi:/hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake fact for the PTP route rather than each carrying their own copy of the disjunction, so a change to one side cannot leave the deduction jumping at the section 199A threshold.
THE OUTER GATE IS DISJUNCTIVE. Everything above is about the INNER gate — which arm of Case 1 a filer takes. The OUTER one is qbi:/claimsQbiDeduction, the first conjunct of Case 1's When and of Case 2's: Any(qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness, qbi:/isEntitledByReitOrPtp), matching Form 8995's own "Who Can Take the Deduction" test, which is DISJUNCTIVE ("You have QBI, qualified REIT dividends, or qualified PTP income or loss") rather than a business-only test. THIS FACT'S OWN SHARE is the line-5 guard inside the REIT/PTP arm: because the outer gate is disjunctive, that arm is reachable by a filer who has no qualified trade or business, and line 5 must be $0 for them — including for one who answered /hasQbiIncome=false while entering a business or filing a Schedule C, whose disowned QBI would otherwise be resurrected by an unrelated Form 1099-DIV. The guard reads qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness, the same fact that guards Form 8995-A line 27 inside qbi:/qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad, so the business half is suppressed on both sides of the section 199A threshold or on neither.
EACH 20 PERCENT PRODUCT IN CASE 1 IS ROUNDED AT ITS OWN LINE. Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 16 box 3 — tax from another form is included in line 16

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 16 box 3 — the write-in form name beside the box

Fact.Name: Section 1341 comparison not computed on this return
Fact.Description:

SCREEN: "You repaid more than $3,000 that was taxed in an earlier year, so your tax is the lower of two methods: deducting the repayment, or a credit for the tax it added in that year. This return has income or tax items (qualified dividends or capital gains, a qualified business income deduction, income averaging of more farm income than your taxable income after the deduction, the foreign earned income exclusion, a community-property allocation, the alternative minimum tax or a nonrefundable credit) for which the two methods cannot yet be compared, so it cannot be filed here."

Fact.Name: Tentative tax from taxable income
Fact.Description:
Tentative tax as reported on line 16 of Form 1040. THREE WORKSHEETS CAN FIGURE THIS LINE. The Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet result (/qdcgLine25 = lesser of the worksheet tax and the ordinary tax), so returns with qualified dividends or net capital gain are taxed at the 0/15/20% preferential rate; for returns with neither, line 25 reduces exactly to the ordinary tax (/ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome), so their tax is unchanged. The SECOND worksheet the same line can require: when Schedule D line 18 or line 19 is more than zero and Schedule D lines 15 and 16 are gains, the Schedule D Tax Worksheet figures this line instead, because it is the only one of the two that carries the 25% unrecaptured-section-1250 and 28%-rate groups. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, the SDTW's own entry test, verbatim: "Complete this worksheet only if line 18 or line 19 of Schedule D is more than zero and lines 15 and 16 of Schedule D are gains ... Otherwise, complete the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet in the instructions for Form 1040, line 16"; and lines 1165-1168, worksheet line 47, "Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16."
THE SWITCH, ARM BY ARM. Arm 0 fires on preferentialRateTax /entersForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheet — the Form 2555 gate AND a non-zero Form 1040 line 15 AND a non-zero Form 2555 lines 45+50 figure, all three printed — and takes preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetTax, that worksheet's line 6. It is complete-safe FALSE on every return that answers nothing, which is what makes inserting it ahead of the two older arms an additions-only change. Arm 1 fires on scheduleD /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet (the entry test as a Derived Boolean, complete-safe FALSE on an unanswered return) and takes scheduleD /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax, worksheet line 47. Arm 2 is the QDCGT body this fact has always had, unchanged character for character, so every gate-false return keeps its exact pre-SDTW value: the whole conformance corpus is gate-false, which is why this VALUE-MOVING change lands as an additions-only delta. The <Round> sits inside each arm, exactly where the arm's own worksheet ends: /qdcgLine25 is unrounded and is rounded here, while /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax already carries the worksheet's single Round, so the Round on arm 1 is idempotent and is kept only so the two arms round at the same syntactic place. Dollar, integer cents, non-negative.
THE SECOND EXCEPTION (:1081-1082) IS RESOLVED BY DOCUMENTED EQUIVALENCE, NOT BY A THIRD ARM, and this is the fact that owes that resolution — scheduleD /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet deliberately assigns it here, because the Exception is a THREE-WAY pre-empt and that gate is only a two-way selector. Verbatim: "Exception: Don't use the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or this worksheet to figure your tax if ... Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15, is zero or less. Instead, see the instructions for Form 1040, line 16." A filer with worksheet gains and zero taxable income therefore belongs to NEITHER arm as drawn. A third arm is not built because all three routes provably agree at $0 and a third arm could only re-derive that $0: /taxableIncome is floored at zero, so (a) the route the Exception names is the Form 1040 line 16 instructions, i.e. the Tax Table, whose lowest row ("at least 0, but less than 5") is $0; (b) the QDCGT's line 24 is the tax on line 1 = the tax on $0 = $0 and line 25 is the smaller of line 23 and line 24, so arm 2 is $0; (c) the SDTW's line 46 is likewise the tax on $0 and line 47 is the smaller of line 45 and line 46, so arm 1 is $0. Leg (c) has one step that is NOT trivially zero and is the one to check: SDTW line 38 collapses to line 10 (the whole preferential income, $6,000 on the pinned case) when line 1 is zero, and line 35 can never exceed line 9, a term of line 10, so line 39 floors at zero and the 25% group contributes nothing. THE PAIR THAT PINS IT: sdtw-gate-zero-taxable-income (gate TRUE) and sdtw-gate-zero-taxable-income-qdcgt-arm (gate FALSE) are the same zero-taxable-income return with and without the box 2d collectibles gain, and both assert this fact at $0. If a later change makes the routes disagree at zero taxable income, that pair fails and the third arm becomes real work.
FORM 2555 IS ARM 0, AND IT IS FIRST. The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet is filled (preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetTax) and Arm 0 routes Form 1040 line 16 to it when preferentialRateTax /entersForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheet fires. ARM ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, not stylistic: that worksheet's own line 4 is what USES the QDCGT or the Schedule D Tax Worksheet, and the SDTW's line 47 redirects away from Form 1040 line 16 for exactly this population (:1167-1168), so a Form 2555 return has to be diverted BEFORE either of the two arms below is reached. The reverse substitution the two worksheets print at their own line 1 (:1084-1086 for the SDTW, the QDCGT's identical carve-out) is the same routing seen from the other end and is likewise satisfied by Arm 0: those worksheets never figure line 16 for a return that takes it.
ARM 0 IS UNREACHABLE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS TODAY, so the paragraph above is not read as more than it says: worksheet line 4's Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet routes, its starred Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet route (preferentialRateTax /feiQdcgLine1-25), and its Schedule D Tax Worksheet route (scheduleD /feiSdtwLine1-46) all COMPUTE, but every Form 2555 return is refused by form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555, unconditionally, for as long as the section 911 computation stays otherwise unbuilt. So this fact is byte-identical on the committed corpus regardless of Arm 0's own correctness.
THE POPULATION IS NOT REACHED BY ARM 1, AND MUST NOT BE. scheduleD /sdtwLine7's Description records a box-2a-only filer (Form 1099-DIV capital gain distributions, no Schedule D filed) for whom the SDTW would OVERSTATE tax relative to the QDCGT, because Schedule D lines 15 and 16 are genuinely blank for such a filer while /qdcgLine3 reads the box-2a total. Arm 1 cannot reach them: the gate requires Schedule D lines 15 AND 16 to exceed zero, which is exactly what that population lacks. This fact does not fix that divergence and does not disturb its documentation; anyone loosening the gate must fix /sdtwLine7 first.
A THIRD ADD TERM: /otherFormTax, the Form 1040 line 16 box 3 write-in amount (the Form 8978, 1291TAX, 965INC and ECR legs), per the printed "Include in the total on the entry space on line 16 all of the following taxes that apply". Complete-safe $0 on a return that enters none of them; it carries its own Round (it stands for the printed write-in space), so this Add still sums already-rounded terms.
THE FORM 8814 LEG. The printed line 16 is not only the worksheet tax: i1040gi's Line 16 says "Include in the total on the entry space on line 16 all of the following taxes that apply", and "Tax from Form(s) 8814" is the second item on that list. form8814:/form8814TotalTax (the sum of Form 8814 line 15 over the elected children) is therefore a term of the Add below, beside the Form 4972 leg that models the third item and the box-3 write-in leg above. It is complete-safe $0 on every return that never opens the election collection, so every committed scenario and every existing fixture keeps its exact value; it carries whole dollars only (each line 15 Rounds itself), so the arm-level Rounds above still sit where each worksheet ends and the Add stays integer-clean. Box 1 (/form8814Included) is derived from the same collection in this module, so the box and the amount can never disagree.
SCHEDULE J MAKES THIS LINE A SELECTOR, AND THE THREE-ARM WORKSHEET SWITCH MOVED. Everything the arm-by-arm paragraphs above describe now lives, character for character, on /regularTaxWithoutScheduleJ; this fact's first term is a two-arm Switch that takes scheduleJ:/scheduleJLine23 when scheduleJ:/scheduleJApplies is true and /regularTaxWithoutScheduleJ otherwise. scheduleJ:/scheduleJApplies is an IsComplete-first gate over its own writable, so it is a complete FALSE on every return that does not elect income averaging and this fact is byte-identical on the committed corpus. The split is not cosmetic: Form 6251 line 10 must use the tax refigured WITHOUT Schedule J, and /line16WithoutScheduleJ is built from the same three-arm fact plus the same Forms 4972 and 8814 and box-3 terms, so the two lines can never drift apart. Every warning above still binds the moved Switch, the one included: anyone loosening the Schedule D Tax Worksheet gate must fix scheduleD:/sdtwLine7 first.

Fact.Description:
Other taxes, including self-employment tax. Schedule 2 line 21 ("Add lines 4, 7 through 16, 18, and 19"), for line 23 of Form 1040.
THE PRINTED COMPOSITION IS EXACTLY "Add lines 4, 7 through 16, 18, and 19": line 4 (Schedule SE), line 7 (schedule2:/line7OfSchedule2, lines 5 + 6), line 8 (form5329:/schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts, every Form 5329 part), line 9 (Schedule H, line 26), line 11 (Additional Medicare Tax, Form 8959), line 12 (Net Investment Income Tax, Form 8960), line 13 (uncollected box-12 tax, formW2s:/schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax), lines 14 to 16, line 18 (schedule2:/line18OfSchedule2, lines 17a through 17z), and line 19. Every term is complete-safe 0 when unanswered, so every committed scenario's line 21 is byte-identical to a return that answers none of them.
THE LINE-13 TERM is the tax that the Schedule 8812 line-22 add-back exists to add back; the charge side is formW2s:/schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax and the favourable add-back half lives as four addends inside ctcOdc:/socialSecurityOverEitc. formW2s:/knockoutBox12Code refuses codes A and M outright; codes B and N reach flow:/flowIsKnockedOut only where the W-2's FICA-vs-RRTA regime is UNDETERMINED — a W-2 that answers the regime files, its uncollected Medicare tax carried on Form 8959 line 19. No committed scenario answers any of the four codes, and the per-W-2 addend is complete-safe 0 when none is answered, so line 13 is 0 on the whole corpus.
THE SCHEDULE H TERM IS LINE 26, NOT LINE 8, and the instruction's chart is the reason: "IF you file Form 1040 or 1040-SR ... THEN enter the amount from Schedule H, line 8 or, if applicable, line 26, on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 9" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sh.pdf, page 7). Line 26 is defined for every filer who reaches Part III and equals line 25 (= line 8) plus a line 16 that is zero for anyone who never entered Part II, so line 26 is the same number the chart names on both of its branches. scheduleH:/scheduleHTotalHouseholdEmploymentTaxes is 0 on every committed scenario (no scenario answers any Schedule H intake), so this addend is additive.

Fact.Name: Total tax
Fact.Description:
Total tax as reported on line 24 of Form 1040: tax after nonrefundable credits (line 22) plus Schedule 2 line 21 other taxes (line 23). Since the Form 8621 module landed, line 24 also SUBTRACTS form8621:/form8621CurrentTaxDeferral, the section 1294 deferred tax of Form 8621 line 9c: the instructions direct the shareholder to subtract that deferred tax from the sum of Form 1040 lines 22 and 23. That sum is /totalTaxBeforeSection1294Deferral, a separate fact rather than an inline Add because Form 8621 line 9a reads the whole return's tax and reading line 24 there would close a cycle. The deferral is complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 8621.
FLOORED AT $0, BELT AND BRACES. form8621:/form8621CurrentTaxDeferral already caps the aggregate of the per-fund Form 8621 line 9c amounts at the tax being deferred, which is the CAUSE of the defect and is where the cap belongs: each fund's line 9a is the WHOLE return's tax, not that fund's share of it, so two or more funds electing under section 1294 produce overlapping 9c amounts whose untrimmed sum exceeds the tax. This floor is the INVARIANT beside it. Form 1040 line 24 is a total tax; nothing the instructions license can make it negative, and a negative line 24 would flow to lines 33, 34 and 37 as a refund of tax never paid. The floor is redundant while the cap holds and is the point at which the return still cannot go wrong if a later change to Form 8621 loosens it.

Fact.Name: Total tax is incomplete
Fact.Description: The total tax calculation is incomplete, so the user cannot file. Form 1040 line 24 is a required entry ("Add lines 22 and 23. This is your total tax"), and the jurat above the signature line obliges the filer to declare the return "true, correct, and complete" — a return whose total tax cannot be resolved cannot honestly carry that declaration, so submission is blocked rather than transmitted with a guessed or missing figure. No dollar direction: nobody is over- or under-charged, because nothing is filed.

Fact.Name: Form 1099 withholding
Fact.Description:
Federal income tax withheld from wages, as reported on line 25b of Form 1040. Adds Form 1099-DIV box 4 (/form1099DivFederalIncomeTaxWithheld); box 4 withholding on the scalar IRA distribution intake (income:/iraDistributionWithholding); and box 4 withholding on the Form 8606 Part I distribution intake for both filers (form8606:/form8606DistributionsWithholding + /spouseForm8606DistributionsWithholding); Form 1099-B box 4 on the Form 8949 transaction rows (scheduleD:/form1099BFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, cents intact); Form 1099-DA box 4 on the received Form 1099-DA items (scheduleD:/form1099DaFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, cents intact); and Form 1099-K box 4 on the Form 1099-K items (income:/form1099KFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, cents intact). Each term is complete-safe 0 when unanswered, so a return answering none of them keeps its line-25b total unchanged.
THE TOTAL IS ROUNDED, because line 25b is a printed, mef-exported whole-dollar entry line. Eight of the nine terms happen to arrive whole (each carries its own Round, at the item or the sub-total), but the ninth does not: socialSecurity:/socialSecurityReports/*/federalTaxWithheld is an unrounded passthrough of a writable Dollar, so an SSA-1099 box 6 (or RRB-1099 box 10) reported as 1,234.56 would put 1234.56 on line 25b and onto its MeF export without this Round.
THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT CLASS FROM SUM-OF-ROUNDED-ADDENDS, and the two must not be confused. Sum-of-rounded-addends is rounding each addend and THEN adding, which yields a whole but wrong total, off by up to ~$0.50 per extra addend. This fact's own defect was the opposite shape: never rounding the total at all, yielding a total that is not a whole dollar. Rounding here is correct regardless of how the other class is handled elsewhere, and it is a PREREQUISITE for any addend that legitimately carries cents: cents-preserving addends are only safe once the line itself rounds.
Zero corpus movement, by construction. Line 25d (/totalWithholding) already wraps its own Add in Round, so the error was never visible downstream of 25d. And the ONLY 25b source that reaches this Add unrounded is the SSA/RRB term: no committed scenario carries cents there, so this Add's input is whole in every committed case and rounding it is a no-op. Note the precise claim — some scenarios DO carry cents at the writable level in other 25b sources (1099-R box 4 at 911.75 and 1507.51 in 1040-withholdings-without-attachments, 1099-MISC box 4 at 314.88 in apf-single-resident-no-dep-withholding), but each of those is rounded by its own item fact or sub-total before it ever reaches line 25b. The guard is pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/socialSecurity/ss-1099-withholding-cents-line25b-rounding, which was authored to exercise the shape the corpus does not.
STILL OPEN: /socialSecurityReports/*/federalTaxWithheld is Export mef="true" and carries cents, unlike its W-2 twin /formW2s/*/federalWithholding, which is Round-wrapped precisely because it stands for one document's printed box. Whether a per-document MeF withholding field must be whole dollars is a separate decision that moves the MeF surface, and it is NEITHER an instance of the sum-of-rounded defect (it carries no Round to remove) NOR repairable without deciding the MeF question first. It needs its own resolution.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's credit for backup withholding (box 13 code B)
Fact.Description:

The form's own page 2 table routes the code in one line, "B Credit for backup withholding Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c", which is /otherFormWithholding below.
THIS IS THE CONSUMER that estimatedPayments:/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box13CreditForEstimatedTaxes was written against: that fact routes code A to Form 1040 line 26 and says in its own Description that code B is deliberately NOT routed there because it belongs to line 25c, a different line of a different total, and that the line 25c consumer must be created in the module that owns Form 1040 line 25. This module owns it. Without this fact the box 13 code B amount would reach nothing at all: a beneficiary whose trust backup-withheld tax for them would lose the credit, which OVERSTATES the tax they owe.
THE SHAPE IS THE CODE A LEG'S, row for row, because both read the same box 13 row list (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/creditEntries). COMPLETE SAFE: a row contributes only when BOTH its code and its amount are answered and the code is B, so a K-1 item that answered no box 13 row contributes a Complete $0. Codes C through G are credits routed to forms this dictionary does not model. Summed over the collection by /otherFormWithholding.

Fact.Description:

Both instructions route it identically: "Include this amount in the total you enter on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c" (i1065sk1, box 15; i1120ssk, box 13) — the SAME line /form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box13BackupWithholding already routes the Form 1041 K-1's code B to, above.

EVERY ROW, whatever the printed row count: the Form 1065 K-1 prints 2 credit rows (box 15), the Form 8865 K-1 prints 4 (box 15) and the Form 1120-S K-1 prints 5 (box 13), and all three are the one row list scheduleE:/formK1s/*/creditEntries, so a row beyond the printed count, listed on the entity's statement, is read like any other.
COMPLETE SAFE, the code A/B leg's own shape: a row contributes only when BOTH its code and its amount are answered and the code is exactly "O" (case sensitive, matching the printed letter); every other code on any row is a credit routed to a form this dictionary does not model (Form 8846, Form 3800, Form 8864, Form 8874, Form 8881, and the rest of the letter list, none of which this fact claims to implement). A K-1 item that answers no credit row contributes a Complete $0. Summed over the collection by /otherFormWithholding below.

Fact.Name: Other Form withholding (Form 1040 line 25c)
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 25c, printed "Other forms (see instructions)" — federal income tax withheld reported on a form OTHER than a W-2 (25a) or a 1099 (25b).
FOUR MODELLED LEGS. Schedule K-1 backup withholding, for every K-1 type this dictionary models: the Form 1041 K-1's code B slots (/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box13BackupWithholding above, whose Description carries the routing quote) and the Form 1065/1120-S K-1's code-O slots (/formK1s/*/k1065And1120sBackupWithholding) — i1040gi's line 25c instruction draws no distinction between a Form 1041 K-1 and a Form 1065/1120-S one ("Federal income tax withheld that is shown on a Schedule K-1" is undifferentiated), so both route here. Form 8959 line 24 Additional Medicare Tax withheld ("Total Additional Medicare Tax withholding. Add lines 22 and 23. Also include this amount with federal income tax withholding on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 25c") and Form W-2G box 4 withholding ("Include on line 25c any Federal income tax withheld on your Form(s) W-2G. The amount withheld should be shown in box 4.") are the other two legs: neither is a W-2 (25a) or a 1099 (25b) amount, so 25c is the only line either can print on.
COMPLETE SAFE AND $0 ON EVERY RETURN THAT ANSWERS NONE OF THEM: each K-1's CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on its own collection defaulting to $0 and each item's term defaults to $0; the 8959 and W-2G legs are each complete-safe in their home modules. /totalWithholding below reads this line, so the credit reaches Form 1040 line 25d, line 33 total payments and the refund.
THIS FACT CARRIES NO ROUND OF ITS OWN, DELIBERATELY. /totalWithholding is Round(Add(25a, 25b, 25c)), so a Round here would round twice. That the printed 25c is a multi-term line with no Round of its own is a STILL OPEN question in the same family as /form1099Withholding's own rounding fix: its only cents-bearing term today is the Schedule K-1 box 13 leg, since the 8959 and W-2G legs each Round themselves, and no committed scenario carries cents on that leg, so this line is whole on the corpus today regardless.
THE FORM 1042-S LEG. i1040gi's line 25c list continues "Tax withheld that is shown on Form 1042-S, Form 8805, or Form 8288-A", so the box 10 total withholding credit of every Form 1042-S on this return is a term of the Add below, through form1042S:/form1042SWithholding (complete-safe zero when no Form 1042-S was entered, so every return without one is unchanged). Forms 8805 and 8288-A printed intake is available. Their income, disposition, claimant eligibility, and withholding treatment remain guarded by /knockoutForm8805TaxTreatmentUnbuilt and /knockoutForm8288ATaxTreatmentUnbuilt; neither form contributes withholding to this Add yet. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Total withholding
Fact.Description:
Total withholding as reported on line 25d of Form 1040: line 25a (W-2 box 2) + line 25b (1099) + line 25c (other forms) — three terms, one per printed line, and nothing else.
THE FORM 8959 AND FORM W-2G LEGS LIVE INSIDE /otherFormWithholding, not directly in this Add: the printed 25c box, which the register maps to /otherFormWithholding, carries the Form 8959 line 24 Additional Medicare Tax withheld and the Form W-2G box 4 withholding as terms of its own Add, and this Add carries them only through it.
IDENTICAL EITHER WAY THE TERMS ARE GROUPED: the two addends sit one level down inside the same Round: Round(25a + 25b + 8959 + w2g + 25c-rest) and Round(25a + 25b + (8959 + w2g + 25c-rest)) are the same expression, so line 25d, line 33 and the refund cannot move depending on which Add carries them. /otherFormWithholding deliberately adds no Round of its own, because a Round there would break this identity; that open question is recorded on that fact. Complete safety holds either way, since the two legs keep their own $0 defaults regardless of which Add they sit in.

Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer qualifies for any nonrefundable credit. If you change the summary table, you must also change this fact. An Incomplete addend (a half-answered Form 1116 behind the foreign tax credit term) makes this predicate Incomplete rather than a silent false, the unanswered-condition posture every other credit flag here already carries; the summary-table gate that reads it treats Incomplete as not-yet-known, never as "no credit".

May be negative when refundable credits exceed total tax. Not exported, and read by no other fact in this dictionary.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 38 as it enters the balance — the penalty, or zero while it is not settled
Fact.Description:
form2210:/form2210FLine16Penalty for a farmer or fisher who files Form 2210-F, else form2210:/form2210Penalty when that fact is COMPLETE, and zero otherwise. The whole content of this fact is the completeness gate, which is why it exists rather than being folded into /balanceDue: the penalty fact has three settled outcomes and two unsettled ones, and only the settled ones may move a balance.
NOT A SILENT ZERO, and the distinction is the same one /form2210Penalty makes. A zero here means "no penalty is being added", which is true both when the penalty is a definite $0 (the filer met one of Form 2210's own no-penalty exits) and when it is not computed at all (Form 2210's default is that the IRS will figure it and bill it). Neither case adds anything to line 37, so one arm serves both — but the fact that DECIDES the amount is /form2210Penalty, which never conflates them.

Fact.Name: Final tax amount
Fact.Description:
The final tax amount -- either a refund or balance based on the positivity of the number. Carries the Form 1040 line 38 penalty leg, on the same footing as /balanceDue: this is the SIGNED net the filer settles, and after line 38 the amount to be settled includes the penalty. Leaving it out would have made /zeroBalance say "nothing to settle" on a return that owes a penalty, while /balanceDue said otherwise.
THE LINE-36 CARRY-FORWARD LEG is the same argument one term further along, and it was MEASURED rather than feared: giving Form 1040 line 36 a real intake made a state reachable that this fact could not read otherwise: a filer who elects to apply the whole overpayment to next year is refunded NOTHING (line 35a is zero) and owes NOTHING, but without this leg the signed net still read minus the overpayment. On three of that unit's six fixtures the result was /dueRefund, /owesBalance AND /zeroBalance all FALSE at once — none of the three exported routing booleans true, which leaves the application with no route at all. That is the same defect class /form1040Line35aRefundAfterEstimatedTaxPenalty was built to remove (there, two of the three true at once), and the fix is one dependency: an overpayment CREDITED forward under IRC 6402(b) is neither refunded nor owed, so it belongs on the tax side of the net.
WHAT THE SIGNED NET NOW IS, EXACTLY: plus the printed line 37 when positive, and minus the printed line 35a when negative. That equivalence is what the leg buys, and it holds in every branch because line 36 is itself ceilinged at line 34 less line 38.
/balanceDue IS PROVABLY UNMOVED and is deliberately not given the same leg. Line 36 is non-zero only when line 34 is, and it never exceeds line 34 less line 38, so /totalTax + line 38 + line 36 never exceeds /totalPayments on any return where line 36 is non-zero — the floored subtraction that is /balanceDue would read zero either way. Adding the term there would say a carry-forward can create a balance due, which it cannot.
EVERY COMMITTED RETURN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: line 36 is zero wherever the line-36 intake is unanswered, and no committed scenario answers it.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 35a "If Form 8888 is attached, check here"
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 35a's checkbox: "Amount of line 34 you want refunded to you. If Form 8888 is attached, check here". TRUE when the Form 8888 split is in effect (form8888:/form8888SplitRefundElected: the filer elected the split, a refund is due, and direct deposit was chosen); complete-safe FALSE on every return that never answers the election, and Incomplete only while a YES waits on the refund or delivery facts it composes with (taxCalculations:/dueRefund, paymentMethod:/refundViaAch still unanswered, a return whose payment section is Incomplete anyway). The intake lives in the form8888 home module (Form 8888 Rev. December 2025, vendored as https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8888.pdf): the election, line 1a, the lines 2-3 additional-account collection, line 5, and the two dual-wired knockouts.
WHAT CHECKING THE BOX CHANGES ON THIS FORM: lines 35b-35d go blank. The instructions make the two an either/or ("Complete lines 35b through 35d (if you want your refund deposited to only one account), or Check the box on line 35a and attach Form 8888"), and paymentMethod:/xmlRefundBankAccount reads this fact to honour it. The refund amount on line 35a itself is unchanged: Form 8888 allocates it, it does not alter it.
NOT A VALUE MOVE ON ANY COMMITTED RETURN: no committed fixture answers the election, and the unanswered election resolves exactly the False this fact used to hard-wire.

Fact.Name: Amount of the overpayment the filer elects to apply to next year's estimated tax
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 36 INTAKE. The printed line asks the filer a question this fact records the answer to: "Amount of line 34 you want applied to your 2026 estimated tax".
A FILER CHOICE, NOT AN ARITHMETIC. The instructions say "Enter on line 36 the amount, IF ANY, of the overpayment on line 34 you want applied to your 2026 estimated tax" — the word "want" is the whole content of the line. Nothing in this graph can derive it, and the $0 this path replaces was an answer given on the filer's behalf.
Integer cents; Min 0. Optional — absent means a complete-safe $0 on line 36, so every committed scenario is unchanged. The clamp against the overpayment lives on /appliedToNextYearEstimated below, NOT on this writable: the filer may answer any number, and it is the printed line that cannot exceed what is available to apply.
TWO CONDITIONS THE PRINTED SPAN STATES THAT THIS INTAKE DOES NOT CARRY, both named as gaps rather than modelled. (1) "We will apply this amount to your account unless you include a statement requesting us to apply it to your spouse's account. Include your spouse's social security number in the statement." — a paper attachment with no Form 1040 line, so this dictionary always applies the amount to the filer's own account. (2) The printed CAUTION, "This election to apply part or all of the amount overpaid to your 2026 estimated tax can't be changed later" — an irrevocability warning the interview must show before it asks; it constrains the application screen, not the arithmetic. Both belong on the application's screen. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Amount Applied To Next Year Estimated (Form 1040 line 36)
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 36, printed "Amount of line 34 you want applied to your 2026 estimated tax". The printed form says 2026; a filer's TY2025 overpayment is applied to the 2026 estimated tax.
The intake is /writableAppliedToNextYearEstimated above; this fact is the PRINTED line, which is the filer's answer CLAMPED to what is actually available to apply.
THE CLAMP IS THE PRINTED IDENTITY, NOT A HOUSE RULE, and it is tighter than "an overpayment cannot be applied beyond itself". The Line 38 instruction states the identity "Lines 35a, 36, and 38 must equal line 34" and then both of its arms: the filer may "subtract the penalty from the amount you would otherwise enter on line 35a or line 36", and "if the penalty is more than the overpayment on line 34, enter -0- on lines 35a and 36". So the ceiling on line 36 is line 34 LESS line 38, floored at zero — not line 34. Clamping only to line 34 would let a filer who elects the whole overpayment print 35a = 0, 36 = line 34 and 38 = the penalty, whose sum is line 34 PLUS the penalty: the printed identity broken on the face of the form. With this ceiling the identity holds by construction on every return WHERE THE INSTRUCTION ASSERTS IT — that is, wherever line 38 does not exceed line 34: below the ceiling, 35a = 34 − 36 − 38 exactly; at the ceiling, 35a floors to 0 and 36 + 38 = 34. Where line 38 DOES exceed line 34 the instruction withdraws the identity itself and substitutes its own arm ("If the penalty is more than the overpayment on line 34, enter -0- on lines 35a and 36. Then, subtract line 34 from line 38 and enter the result on line 37"), and this ceiling is 0 there, which is that arm's first half; /balanceDue carries its second.
THIS DISCHARGES THE STANDING INSTRUCTION /form1040Line35aRefundAfterEstimatedTaxPenalty left for whoever added the intake ("the unit that adds that intake must revisit THIS fact and not only add a writable"). Line 35a keeps its body unmodified and is now correct for a non-zero line 36 as well, because the -0- arm is honoured inside line 36 rather than being left to line 35a's floor; see that fact's Description, amended in the same unit.
THIS DICTIONARY STILL TAKES THE WHOLE PENALTY OUT OF LINE 35a, which the instruction's "line 35a OR line 36" makes a filer's choice and which nothing asks. That is a named gap, not a modelled preference: a filer who would rather preserve the carry-forward and shrink the refund gets the same total either way, but a different split across the two printed lines.
ROUNDED, like line 34 and line 35a beside it, so the three printed lines and line 38 are whole dollars and their identity is exact in the printed units. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 35a — the refund actually paid out, after the line-38 penalty comes out of the overpayment
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 35a, "Amount of line 34 you want refunded to you". Line 34 (/overpayment) is what the filer OVERPAID; this is what is actually sent back after the Form 1040 line 38 estimated-tax penalty has been taken out of it.
THE ARITHMETIC IS THE INSTRUCTION'S ARMS (2) AND (3) AT ONCE, the same collapse /balanceDue makes for arm (1) — see the block note above. "However, if you have an overpayment on line 34, subtract the penalty from the amount you would otherwise enter on line 35a or line 36" is the subtraction; "if the penalty is more than the overpayment on line 34, enter -0- on lines 35a and 36" is the floor at zero. So line 35a = max(0, line 34 − line 36 − line 38), and the printed identity "lines 35a, 36, and 38 must equal line 34" holds by construction for every filer whose penalty does not exceed the overpayment.
LINE 34 IS STILL NOT TOUCHED. /overpayment stays the printed line 34 and stays mef-exported unchanged; the penalty is a USE of the overpayment, not a reduction of it. That is the same reading /balanceDue records, and this fact is its other half: the reduction of the refund now lands somewhere instead of being unrepresented.
WHAT THIS FIXES, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. Until this fact existed /dueRefund read line 34, so a filer whose overpayment was wholly consumed by the penalty exported /dueRefund TRUE and /owesBalance TRUE at the same time — two contradictory claims about one return, both carried downstream to the application. For example, on a constructed return (total tax 3,875, withholding 500, $3,475 paid with the extension request, penalty 154 → overpayment 100 and balance due 54) exported both booleans true, while paymentMethod:/xmlRefundDisbursementCd on that same return already said 0, "Balance Due/Zero Balance".
THE COHERENCE INVARIANT THIS ESTABLISHES IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A HOPE. Write P for the line-38 leg (/estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg), T for /totalTax and Y for /totalPayments; line 36 is zero unless the filer elected a carry-forward, and never exceeds line 34 less P. /overpayment = max(0, Y − T) and /balanceDue = max(0, T + P − Y). If Y is at least T, then line 35a > 0 says (Y − T) > P while /owesBalance says P > (Y − T), and both cannot hold. If Y is less than T, line 34 is 0, so line 35a is 0 and /dueRefund is false outright. Hence /dueRefund and /owesBalance can NEVER both be true; and when the penalty exactly equals the overpayment both are false and /zeroBalance is true, so exactly one of the three holds on every return. A future non-zero line 36 only shrinks line 35a further, so it cannot break the direction of this argument.
REACHABLE, AND NARROWLY — which is why zero committed returns exercise it. A withholding-driven overpayment is SELF-EXEMPTING: withholding big enough to overpay makes Form 2210 line 7 (line 4 − line 6) negative, which is less than $1,000, which is the de-minimis exit, which makes /form2210Penalty a definite $0. So the overpayment must come from money Form 1040 line 33 counts and Form 2210 line 6 does not — a Schedule 3 payment or a refundable credit — and the two deliberate conservatisms in estimatedPayments (line 4 does not subtract 2210 line 3, line 6 omits Schedule 3 line 11) are exactly what keep that money out of the exemption test. The witnesses use Schedule 3 line 10, the amount paid with the extension request: a filer who paid nothing in during the year and then overshot on Form 4868 overpays line 34 and still owes the section 6654 penalty, because a payment made on April 15, 2026 earns no day-count credit in a penalty that accrues to that same date.
LINE 36 IS NOT IDENTICALLY ZERO. The intake exists: /writableAppliedToNextYearEstimated, clamped onto the printed line by /appliedToNextYearEstimated. The two consequences it named are settled where they belong — in that fact, not here. FIRST: the instruction's "subtract the penalty from the amount you would otherwise enter on line 35a OR line 36" is a filer CHOICE, nothing asks it, and this dictionary still takes the whole penalty out of line 35a. That is now a NAMED GAP rather than the only available answer. SECOND: the arm that says "enter -0- on lines 35a AND 36" is honoured by line 36's own ceiling, which is line 34 less line 38 floored at zero, so line 36 can never arrive here at a value the identity cannot carry.
THE BODY BELOW IS UNCHANGED AND IS CORRECT FOR A NON-ZERO LINE 36, which is the claim this unit had to make good rather than assume. Because line 36 never exceeds line 34 less line 38, the Subtract is non-negative whenever line 34 is at least line 38; where it is not, line 36 is zero and the GreaterOf floor does exactly what it did before. The coherence argument above is likewise unaffected: it already allowed for a non-zero line 36 and said so ("A future non-zero line 36 only shrinks line 35a further").
NOT MEF-EXPORTED, DELIBERATELY. Line 35a has an MeF element, but claiming that mapping is not this repo's business (invariant #7 — the application owns the wire format), and the shape this fill had to fix was a downstream-facts contradiction, not a missing MeF field. The export is downstreamFacts only, matching /dueRefund, the fact it feeds.

Fact.Name: Due refund
Fact.Description:
Is the taxpayer due a refund? Reads Form 1040 line 35a — the refund actually paid out — and NOT line 34, the overpayment. The distinction bites only when the line-38 estimated-tax penalty eats into the overpayment, and it is the whole reason line 35a exists: while this fact read line 34 it resolved TRUE on returns where /owesBalance also resolved TRUE, and both are exported downstream. /form1040Line35aRefundAfterEstimatedTaxPenalty carries the identity that now makes the two mutually exclusive; /zeroBalance is the third leg, and exactly one of the three holds on every return.
UNMOVED FOR EVERY COMMITTED RETURN, measured rather than assumed: line 35a equals line 34 whenever the line-38 leg is zero, and /form2210Penalty is Complete and non-zero on exactly one of the 939 committed cases, a return that owes the penalty, whose overpayment is zero and whose /dueRefund stays false.

Fact.Name: Balance due
Fact.Description:
The amount that total taxes exceed total payments, plus the Form 1040 line 38 estimated-tax penalty. Reported on line 37 of Form 1040.
THE LINE-38 LEG IS ALL THREE PRINTED ARMS AT ONCE — see the block note above. Adding the penalty inside the floored subtraction gives "add the penalty to any tax due" when there is no overpayment, zero when the overpayment covers it, and "subtract line 34 from line 38" when the penalty exceeds it, without a Switch. Line 34 (/overpayment) is deliberately unchanged: the instruction's identity is that lines 35a, 36 and 38 must EQUAL line 34, so the penalty is a use of the overpayment rather than a reduction of it.
UNMOVED FOR EVERY RETURN WHOSE PENALTY IS NOT SETTLED, because /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg is zero unless /form2210Penalty is Complete — Incomplete on the 419 returns this dictionary declines to compute a penalty for, and Placeholder on four whose /totalTax is itself provisional.

Fact.Name: Section 1 tax without income averaging
Fact.Description:
The section 1 tax on /taxableIncome figured WITHOUT the Schedule J election: the three-arm worksheet Switch that /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome carried until Schedule J arrived, moved here character for character. Arm 0 is the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet, arm 1 the Schedule D Tax Worksheet, arm 2 the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet; the arm-by-arm reasoning, the Exception at zero taxable income and the warning about loosening the Schedule D Tax Worksheet gate are all on /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome and all bind this Switch.
TWO CONSUMERS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS ITS OWN FACT. /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome (Form 1040 line 16) takes it whenever the filer does not elect income averaging, and /line16WithoutScheduleJ takes it always, because the 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 line 10 require the regular tax refigured without Schedule J. Building the second out of the first would be impossible: the election is already inside line 16.
NOT the whole of line 16. The Form 4972 lump-sum tax, the Form 8814 tax and the box-3 write-in are added OUTSIDE this fact, on line 16 and on /line16WithoutScheduleJ alike.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 16 recomputed without Schedule J
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 16 as it would read if the filer had NOT elected income averaging: /regularTaxWithoutScheduleJ plus the same three terms the printed line adds beside the worksheet tax — the Form 4972 lump-sum tax, the Form 8814 tax on a child's income, and the box-3 write-in /otherFormTax.
ITS ONE CONSUMER IS FORM 6251 LINE 10. The 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 require a filer who used Schedule J to figure line 16 to refigure that tax, INCLUDING any tax from Form 8814, without using Schedule J before completing line 10, and only for Form 6251 — the printed Form 1040 line 16 is not changed. Keeping the Form 8814 term is therefore not an option but the instruction's own words, and keeping the Form 4972 and box-3 terms keeps this fact the same quantity line 16 is, term for term, minus the election.
On every return that does not elect income averaging this fact and /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome are the same number, which is why the whole committed corpus is byte-identical across the split.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 lines 22 plus 23 before QEF deferral
Fact.Description:
The sum of Form 1040 line 22 (tax after nonrefundable credits) and line 23 (Schedule 2 line 21 other taxes) — the quantity printed line 24 used to be, before the section 1294 deferral was subtracted from it.
IT IS A SEPARATE FACT TO KEEP THE GRAPH ACYCLIC, and that is the whole reason it exists. Form 8621 line 9a is "the total tax on your total taxable income", i.e. this sum; line 9c is the deferred tax figured from it; and line 24 is this sum minus the aggregate of the line 9c amounts. If /totalTax carried the Add inline, Form 8621 would have to read /totalTax to figure the deferral that /totalTax subtracts, and the Fact Graph resolves on edges, not on values.
Its second consumer is form8621:/form8621CurrentTaxDeferral's cap: the aggregate deferral is trimmed to this amount, which is what keeps line 24 from going below zero when two or more funds elect under section 1294 and their overlapping line 9c amounts sum past the tax being deferred.

Fact.Description: Forms 8805 received for tax year 2025, one item per statement. Fact.Name: Form 8805 credit claimant on this return
